headline: CREATOR ADVERTISING SCORES 99 OUT OF 100 ON THE NUMBER THAT SETS BUDGETS, AND 151 ON THE ONE THAT DOES NOT.  THAT GAP IS WHY THE WORK KEEPS GETTING CUT WHILE IT IS WORKING
deck: Meta published a 54-page paper on creator measurement on Wednesday, and the number holding it up is not Meta's.  It belongs to the IPA, and it has been sitting in public for a year.  Read it once and the whole pattern of brands trying creators, liking the results and quietly trimming the line makes sense.
tldr: Creator marketing indexes 99 on short-term return against an all-channel average of 100, and 151 on long-term return with the highest multiplier the IPA measured, so the work gets cut on the number budgets use and wins on the number they do not.  Commission long-term modelling on your last three creator campaigns now, so an answer exists before the next budget round.

Meta's own 20-study test reports a 45 percent lower median cost per extra purchase when at least 30 percent of a test cell's creative assets run from the creator's own account rather than the brand's, at 92 percent confidence.  Count what share of your live assets run from creator handles today and write a target share into the next brief.

RTL put more than 200 episodes of a 1996 police show on YouTube free, drew 30 million views from an audience that is 83 percent men averaging 30, and reports a 26 percent rise in subscriptions linked to that same show.  Pick the title in your library with no commercial value left and release a full season free with a clear route to the newer episodes.

The advert that cost Good Good five commercial partnerships and its chief executive in twelve days moved its subscriber count from 2.12 million up to 2.16 million, because the audience and the partners are separate risks.  Name one person with explicit veto authority over every creator-produced asset and put the name in the statement of work.

An esports season lost 4.6 percent of its hours watched while its average audience rose 72 percent, because the airtime was cut almost in half.  Ask for airtime in hours beside every hours-watched figure in your live proposals, and price on average concurrent viewers instead.

The 60 seconds of sponsor read inside a long-form video is the only reusable asset the deal produces, and a standard contract buys one placement in one video.  Add a clip rights clause to your next creator contract, then cut that segment so it stands alone with its own opening and a clean exit.

From 21 October, certified online gambling operators can buy the YouTube homepage Masthead, on a notice that names no countries.  Ask your Google representative in writing this week what gambling creative can appear on that surface in your markets and whether you can exclude it.
